water.coagulant_delivery_loss.name: Coagulant metering-pump delivery loss
water.coagulant_delivery_loss.summary: Delivered coagulant dose drifting below the jar-test target while the raw water holds steady, with the metering pump losing discharge pressure and stroke stability at the same setting — a worn diaphragm or slipping check valves, not a setpoint change.

pipeline.title: Expected dose

pipeline.title: Raw water

pipeline.title: The pump
pipeline.text: delivered flow and discharge pressure against their own first 90 minutes

pipeline.title: Downstream
pipeline.text: jar-test deviation, floc formation and settled-water turbidity, one residence time behind

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: all required checks → raise; an independent check agrees → medium; recalibration done and the dose back on target → high

peers.use: each train has its own jar-test optimum and dose setpoint, so peers are used for the shape of the drift, not its level

residual below −drop_pct for sustain_min
raw turbidity within ±raw_band_pct of its baseline over the episode

jar-test deviation > jar_limit_pct
settled-water turbidity up > settled_rise_ntu, starting at least lag_min after the dose fell

pipeline.text: all required checks → raise; the blanket falls after an extra cycle → high

water.settled_turbidimeter_fault.summary: A settled-water turbidimeter swinging by whole NTU between one five-minute sample and the next, while the filter it feeds, the blanket under it, the dose ahead of it and the other five basins all stay flat. Nothing physical can move that fast and leave no trace.

water.raw_turbidity_shock.summary: Raw turbidity at one intake rising several times over in under two hours, confirmed by the screen and the rake on the same channel, and then working its way down the train — coagulant demand, settled water, the filters and chlorine demand, each one stage behind the last.

pipeline.title: Rate

pipeline.title: The channel agrees

pipeline.title: Other intakes

pipeline.title: Cascade

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: raw water plus the mechanical signals → real shock; the chain and the recovery → high

peers.use: rule out a plant-wide analyser or calculation change; each train draws through its own screen and channel

ruleOut: solids stirred up by the raw-water pumps

water.filter_backwash_cycling.name: Filter backwashing more often than its cycle
water.filter_backwash_cycling.summary: A filter washing every forty minutes instead of every two days. Each wash is textbook — headloss resets, the pump runs, the bed ripens and the water is clean — so nothing alarms; the finding is the count, and the fact that each run ends far below terminal headloss.

pipeline.title: Find the washes
pipeline.text: headloss resets bigger than reset_drop_ft, confirmed by the backwash pump

pipeline.title: Count
pipeline.text: how many in the last window_min, against this filter's own normal cycle

pipeline.title: Each one normal
pipeline.text: headloss back near its clean value and effluent back in spec within recover_min

pipeline.title: Why so soon
pipeline.text: headloss at the moment each wash starts, against terminal headloss

pipeline.title: Cost
pipeline.text: projected run length, unit filter run volume, backwash cycles per day

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: repeated complete washes on one filter → raise; the pump data agrees → medium

peers.use: how often a healthy filter on this water washes

expected.fitOn: this filter's own projected cycle before the washes started

headloss climbs more than reload_ratio × its pre-event rate between washes

water.ct_margin_loss.name: CT margin narrowing
water.ct_margin_loss.summary: Disinfection credit running out of margin: CT actual falling toward CT required because the contact basin has lost usable volume, with the free chlorine residual unchanged. Healthy equipment, a compliance number to watch.

pipeline.title: Margin
pipeline.text: CT actual against CT required, as a percentage

pipeline.title: Rate
pipeline.text: how fast CT is falling, and how long the margin lasts at that rate

pipeline.title: Split it
pipeline.text: CT = residual × T₁₀, so compare the change in each: C against T

pipeline.title: The limit
pipeline.text: CT required, which moves with temperature and pH

pipeline.title: The basin
pipeline.text: contact basin level and residence time; and the flow, which also shortens contact time

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: margin thin, falling, and all of it contact time → raise; the maintenance record → high

peers.use: the margin the rest of the plant is holding on the same water temperature and pH

expected.formula: free chlorine residual × T₁₀ × k; the margin is CT actual ÷ CT required − 1

checks.rule: CT actual ÷ CT required − 1 < margin_pct
at the last slope_window_min rate, CT reaches CT required within project_min
the margin has been under margin_pct for sustain_min
contact time down > time_drop_pct while the residual stays within ±res_band_pct
CT required within ±req_band_pct of its baseline
contact basin level down > level_drop_pct and residence time down with it
train throughput within ±flow_band_pct of its baseline
chlorine feed pump steady — the residual is being held, not chased
every other train's margin is more than peer_gap_pct points wider than this one's
a maintenance record on this basin in the hour before the fall

ruleOut: a colder or higher-pH water raising the required CT
a CT calculation or analyser change across the plant

conclusion.label: Cause
conclusion.text: The T02 coagulant metering pump lost delivery — worn diaphragm or slipping check valves — so the dose fell −15 % below the jar-test target; recalibration at 11:38 put it back
conclusion.confidenceText: Confirmed by inspection and by the dose coming back

series.label: Jar-test target for this raw water

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: T02 delivered coagulant dose against the jar-test target for the raw water at the time. The shaded gap is coagulant the water did not get.

checks.label: Dose below the jar-test target for this raw water
checks.value: 15.4 mg/L at 11:30 against 18.0 mg/L expected (−14.5 %). The flag level is −10 %.
checks.why: Coagulant dose is set from a jar test and paced to flow. At a steady raw water the target does not move, so a falling delivered dose means the water is being under-dosed.

checks.label: Held low, not one bad sample
checks.value: Below −10 % since 11:05 (20 min by 11:25); first below −4 % at 10:40.
checks.why: Needs 20 min below the flag level, so a single sample or a flow-pacing wobble cannot raise it.

checks.label: Raw water unchanged, so the target has not moved
checks.value: Raw turbidity 7.7–9.1 NTU through the episode against 8.1 NTU this morning (at most 12 % off; the band is ±40 %).
checks.why: The jar-test optimum rises with raw turbidity. With the raw water flat, nothing justifies less coagulant — this is lost delivery, not a re-optimised dose.

checks.label: The metering pump is delivering less at the same setting
checks.value: Pumped flow 1.72 gpm over the last 30 min against 1.97 gpm this morning (−12.7 %), discharge pressure 15.03 psi against 16.22 psi (−7.3 %).
checks.why: A diaphragm that has lost its seal, or check valves that slip, move less liquid per stroke and build less pressure. A lowered setpoint would cut the flow with the pressure unchanged.

checks.label: Stroke stability falling with it
checks.value: 93.9 at its lowest against 96.9 this morning (−3.0 points; the flag is −1.5).
checks.why: A separate measurement on the pump. Stroke-to-stroke delivery gets ragged as a diaphragm hardens or a valve seat leaks, before the average dose has moved far.

checks.label: Bench jar test disagrees with the plant
checks.value: Jar-test deviation 6.8 % at 11:30 against 4.0 % this morning; the limit is 6 %.
checks.why: The jar test is a bench measurement with its own sample and operator. It says the dose in the water is the wrong one, independently of the dosing instruments.

checks.label: Settled water turbidity followed, one residence time behind
checks.value: 2.99 NTU at 11:30 against 2.15 NTU this morning (+0.84 NTU), 50 min after the dose started to fall.
checks.why: A different sensor, a stage downstream. Under-dosed water makes weaker floc that settles worse, and it shows up after flocculation and settling, not at once.

checks.label: Floc formation poorer in the rapid mix
checks.value: Floc formation index 77 at its lowest against 88 this morning (−11 points).
checks.why: Too little metal salt leaves particles charged and they do not stick. The index drops with the dose and comes back with it.

checks.label: Comparable trains dosed to target
checks.value: T01, T05 and T06: at worst −6.4 % off their own expected dose over the same window, inside ±5 %.
checks.why: All six trains share the coagulant storage, the raw water source and the jar-test schedule. Only this train lost dose, so the chemical and the lab work are not the problem.

checks.label: Dose back on target after the pump was worked on
checks.value: "Inspect coagulant feed pump" completed 11:38; residual back inside ±6 % from 11:45 and held 2 h 25 min.
checks.why: The strongest test there is: the dose came back the moment the pump was recalibrated, with nothing else touched.

references.title: Metering-pump diaphragm wear
references.description: The diaphragm hardens and loses its seal. Delivery per stroke falls a little every hour, discharge pressure sags with it, and the dose drifts below target until someone checks it against the calibration column.
notes: Same slow, continuous loss of delivery
Pressure falling with the flow
Found and corrected by recalibration

charts.title: Dose against target (h from the first drift)

references.title: Check valves slipping on grit
references.description: Grit or crystallised coagulant holds a ball check off its seat. Delivery drops in steps as the valve re-seats and slips again, rather than drifting, and a flush often restores it.
notes: Steps rather than a drift
Worth flushing the valves before rebuilding the head

charts.title: Dose against target (h from the first drift)

references.title: Someone lowered the dose setpoint
references.description: A jar test finds a lower optimum, the operator lowers the setpoint, and the dose steps down and stays there. Nothing is wrong: the pump still makes its pressure and strokes cleanly.
notes: Today the dose drifted over 50 min instead of stepping
Discharge pressure fell −7.3 % — a setpoint change leaves it flat

charts.title: Dose against target (h from the first drift)

ruledOut.cause: A raw-water change moving the jar-test optimum
ruledOut.reason: Raw turbidity stayed 7.7–9.1 NTU and pH 7.28–7.40 through the episode. The target the dose is judged against moved less than 1 %.

ruledOut.cause: An operator or controller setpoint change
ruledOut.reason: Discharge pressure fell −7.3 % and stroke stability −3.0 points while the flow fell. Turning a pump down does not make it lose pressure or stroke unevenly.

ruledOut.cause: Coagulant tank low, or a weak batch
ruledOut.reason: Storage tank level 67–74 % all shift, and the other five trains dose from the same chemical with no drift.

ruledOut.cause: A faulty dose transmitter (the dose is really on target)
ruledOut.reason: The water agrees with the reading: settled turbidity rose +0.84 NTU and the bench jar test came out 6.8 % off. A reading-only fault leaves both flat.
A plugged injector shows the same dose loss but with discharge pressure *rising*, and here it fell. The inspection covers both; the injection quill is worth a look while the head is open.

WSIT01.excluded: Left out of the train comparison: T03 and T04 — their own raw turbidity moved more than ±40 % in this window, so their jar-test target moved with it and a dose gap there means something different.

confidence.because: The dose shortfall, the pump's own flow and pressure, the bench jar test and the settled-water turbidimeter are four separate measurements and all four point at the pump. The pump was opened at 11:38 and the dose returned to target straight after.
confidence.lowerIf: The calibration column draws down exactly as set. Then suspect the dose transmitter or the injection point rather than the pump.
confidence.confirmedBy: Pump inspection and recalibration at 11:38, dose back to 17.9 mg/L

action.text: Recalibrate the coagulant feed pump and confirm dose against a fresh jar test before returning to automatic control.

model.fittedOn: T02's own first 1 h 30 min; the exponent is the weak rise of the jar-test optimum with raw turbidity

WSIT01.impact: About 1 h of water treated below the jar-test target, worst −15 %. Settled water reached 2.99 NTU against 2.2 NTU normally on this train; filter effluent stayed at 0.08 NTU, well inside the 0.3 NTU limit, so no finished-water exceedance.

conclusion.label: Cause
conclusion.text: Solids into the T04 basin went up (+42 % raw turbidity) while the desludge cycle stretched +68 %, so the blanket gained 19 points in 1 h 25 min; an extra cycle brought it back
conclusion.confidenceText: Confirmed: the blanket fell as soon as an extra cycle ran

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: T04 sludge blanket against the level it held while solids in and solids out were in balance. Carryover starts around 45 %; the weir is at 70 %.

checks.label: Blanket climbing, not sitting still
checks.value: +13.7 % of basin depth per hour at 11:25 (39.0 % at 10:45 → 48.0 % at 11:25). The flag rate is 8 %/h.
checks.why: A blanket in balance sits at one level: what settles into it is swept out by the collector. A steady climb means more is coming in than is going out.

checks.label: Above the level where floc starts to carry over
checks.value: 48.0 % of basin depth at 11:25, peak 58.0 % at 12:10, against 34.7 % this morning. Carryover starts around 45 %.
checks.why: Below about 45 % the blanket is a filter that helps. Above it, floc is close enough to the launder to be pulled over the weir with the settled water.

checks.label: The rise held
checks.value: Rising faster than 8 %/h since 10:55 (30 min by 11:25).
checks.why: Needs 30 min of it. A collector pass or a stirred sample can lift one reading; it cannot hold a trend.

checks.label: Not a basin-level artefact
checks.value: Sedimentation basin level 90.2–93.2 % against 90.3 % this morning — at most 3.3 % off, which could account for 1.1 of the 9.0 points the blanket gained.
checks.why: The blanket is measured as a share of basin depth. A lower water level would make it read higher with no more sludge in the basin — but only in proportion, and the numbers do not come close.

checks.label: The other five basins steady
checks.value: T01, T02, T03, T05 and T06: at most +1.7 points between 10:45 and 11:25, against +9.0 points here.
checks.why: All six basins share the source water, the coagulant and the desludge schedule. Only this one is filling up, so it is this basin's balance that changed.

checks.label: Desludge cycle running slower than it was
checks.value: Collector cycle time 25.4 min at 12:10 against 15.1 min this morning (+68 %). The flag is +15 %.
checks.why: Cycle time is how long between sweeps to the hopper. Stretch it and less sludge leaves per hour, whatever is settling out.

checks.label: More solids coming in
checks.value: Raw turbidity averaged 10.6 NTU since 10:45 against 7.5 NTU at shift start (+42 %).
checks.why: The intake analyser, upstream and independent. More turbidity in means more floc settling out per hour, so the same desludge cycle falls behind.

checks.label: Collector working harder
checks.value: Collector motor current 6.0 A at 11:10 against 5.6 A this morning (+7 %), read before any extra cycle so raised travel speed is not in it.
checks.why: A separate sensor, on the drive. A deeper, denser blanket is heavier to drag, so the current rises with the blanket — which also says the blanket is real, not a reading.

checks.label: Settled water starting to carry floc
checks.value: Settled turbidity 2.48 NTU at 12:10 against 2.00 NTU this morning (+0.49 NTU).
checks.why: The consequence that matters: floc leaving over the weir loads the filters. It moves only once the blanket is high, which is what the blanket level predicted.

checks.label: The blanket dropped as soon as an extra cycle ran
checks.value: Collector travel speed up to 88 % from 12:10 (normally 57 %); blanket 58.0 % → 44.5 % by 12:25 and 34.4 % now.
checks.why: Desludging is the only thing that was changed, and the blanket came down within minutes. That closes the mass balance: the way out was the problem.

references.title: Desludging left behind by the solids load
references.description: Raw turbidity steps up, the auto-cycle timer stays where it was, and the blanket climbs at a near-constant rate for hours. An extra cycle at raised travel speed pulls it straight back down, and the timer is re-set for the new loading.
notes: Same straight climb
Same cure: one extra cycle
Timer worth re-checking against raw turbidity

charts.title: Sludge blanket (h from the start of the rise)

references.title: Collector drive slipping or chain jammed
references.description: The same rise, but from the other side of the balance: the collector is cycling on time and simply is not moving sludge. Travel speed drops away and motor current spikes or collapses.
notes: Here cycle time stretched +68 % — the drive was running, just not often enough
Check travel speed and current before the timer

charts.title: Sludge blanket (h from the start of the rise)

references.title: Solids surge the desludging kept up with
references.description: Raw turbidity rises the same way, but the cycle shortens with it. The blanket lifts a few points and flattens below the carryover level. Nothing to do.
notes: Today the blanket went to 58.0 %, not a few points
There the cycle time came down; here it went up

charts.title: Sludge blanket (h from the start of the rise)

ruledOut.reason: T01, T02, T03, T05 and T06 all held their blankets within +1.7 points on the same source water while this one gained +9.0.

ruledOut.cause: A basin level change making the blanket read high
ruledOut.reason: Basin level stayed within 3.3 % of 90.3 %, worth 1.1 points of blanket reading against the 9.0 points it actually gained.
It kept running the whole time: travel speed 52–88 % and current 4.5–7.7 A. The cycle got longer, not absent.
Weir overflow rate stayed within 2.7 % of 17,160 gpd/ft (band ±3 %), so the basin was not being pushed harder.
Two other things agree with it: collector current rose +7 % as the blanket thickened, and settled turbidity rose +0.49 NTU once it passed 45 %.

confidence.because: Both sides of the balance are measured: the intake analyser shows more solids arriving and the collector shows longer gaps between sweeps. The blanket, the collector current and the settled-water turbidimeter are three separate instruments and all three moved together. An extra cycle at 12:10 reversed it within 15 min.
confidence.lowerIf: The blanket keeps rising after an extra cycle. Then the collector is not clearing the hopper — check the drive, the chain and the sludge line.
confidence.confirmedBy: Blanket 58.0 % → 44.5 % after the extra cycle at 12:10

action.text: Run an extra desludge cycle and re-check the auto-cycle timer logic against current raw water turbidity.

model.formula: 34.7 % of basin depth, the level it held while in balance

WSIT02.impact: At +13.7 %/h the blanket would have reached the weir at 70 % in about 1 h 36 min, around 13:01. It peaked at 58.0 % and was back to 34.4 % by 14:05; settled turbidity gave up +0.49 NTU on the way and filter effluent never moved.

conclusion.label: Most likely cause
conclusion.text: Resistance building inside the T01 filter bed — mudballs or lost media depth — climbing 4.5× faster than the other filters while the filtered water stays clean
conclusion.confidenceText: Headloss and the bed's own ΔP agree

series.label: At the other filters' rate (0.07 ft/h)

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: T01 filter headloss against what the same run would have cost at the other filters' rate. The gap is resistance the solids load does not explain.

chart.title: What we see

checks.label: Raw turbidity 7.6× its baseline
checks.value: 68.1 NTU at 12:00 against 9.0 NTU before the event (7.6×). The flag is 2.0×.
checks.why: Runoff after rain carries the catchment's silt into the river. A plant sized for 8–11 NTU has to treat several times that, and every barrier downstream feels it.

checks.label: Arrived at storm speed
checks.value: +24 NTU/h over the hour to 11:20, peaking at +52 NTU/h; 11.3 → 68.1 NTU in 1 h 20 min.

checks.value: Screen ΔP 2.02 psi against 1.46 psi before (+38 %), rake torque 69 % against 50 % (+37 %).
checks.why: Two mechanical measurements, nothing to do with the turbidimeter. Debris and silt blind the screen, which costs head and makes the rake work harder. That is real water, not a reading.

checks.value: pH 6.98 at the worst against 7.31 before (−0.33); intake flow variability 4.7 against 2.7.

checks.label: The other five intakes did not see it
checks.value: Worst elsewhere: 1.50× baseline on T04, against 7.6× here. Each train draws through its own screen and channel.

checks.label: Coagulant dose raised to match
checks.value: 23.9 mg/L at 12:20 against 18.3 mg/L baseline (+31 %), first raised at 11:50 — 1 h 10 min into the event.

checks.label: The barriers downstream held

checks.why: If the residual were being held up against a rising demand, the feed pump would be working harder. It is not — so there is headroom to raise the residual deliberately if the margin gets thinner.

checks.label: The other five trains keep their usual margin
checks.value: T01 +17 %, T03 +23 %, T04 +22 %, T05 +21 % and T06 +22 % against +6.7 % here, on the same water temperature and pH — every one of them at least 11 points wider.
checks.why: All six trains disinfect the same water with the same required CT. Only this basin lost margin, which is where a plant-wide cause would have shown.

checks.label: Planned work logged on this basin
checks.value: "Contact basin baffle maintenance started." logged at 13:00, when the basin was 90 % full; it is 74 % now, and contact time was measurably short by 13:20.
checks.why: The maintenance log, not telemetry. It explains the lost volume and tells the operator the margin comes back when the work finishes — this is a planned consequence, not a fault.

references.title: Baffle work with the residual raised first
references.description: The crew takes a bay out, contact time drops, and the operator lifts the free chlorine residual by a couple of tenths before the work starts. CT dips and then flattens well clear of the required value, and the margin never gets interesting.

confidence.because: CT is a product of two measured numbers and the split is unambiguous: contact time −16.0 %, residual +1.4 %, CT −14.7 %. The basin level and residence time, two instruments on the basin, agree that volume is out of service, and the maintenance log puts planned baffle work on this basin at 13:00.
confidence.lowerIf: The basin level comes back without any work being recorded. Then the level instrument or a valve line-up is the thing to check, not the baffles.
confidence.confirmedBy: Maintenance log: "Contact basin baffle maintenance started." at 13:00

action.text: Monitor CT each 15-minute cycle until baffle maintenance completes; increase residual slightly if the margin narrows further.

WSIT07.impact: Margin 30 → 8 CT units in 45 min, +6.7 % above the required value against +22 % on the other trains. Still compliant every sample so far. Raising the residual from 1.22 to 1.32 mg/L would restore a 15 % margin at the present contact time; so would cutting the flow.
